Pulse for 30 October 2026

The stories from 30 October 2026 in the Pulse of the Sapaude app, in our own words. Terms you don’t know are explained in the glossary. Glossary

Device

First AI answer from orbit

A TPU is a chip Google builds for AI math, and the company's research blog says a prototype satellite has returned the first reply from a data-center-class chip of that kind while in orbit.

Everyday tool

Opt out of AI training

A policy token is a shared name in robots.txt, the small file a website already uses to talk to programs that copy pages, and on 30 October 2026 Google, Microsoft, and OpenAI said they plan to honor one name as a request to leave a site out of generative AI training.

AI agents

Agents steer the telescope

An agent is a piece of software that can carry out steps with tools, and on 30 October 2026 NVIDIA said agents at the Allen Telescope Array in Northern California can steer that instrument from one request in ordinary language.

AI agents

Apps can add clicking AI

Computer Use is a tool in Google's Gemini API that lets a developer's program show a model a screenshot and receive the next click, and the release notes of 30 October 2026 call that tool generally available.

In the background

ChatGPT ends violent chats

ChatGPT is a chat assistant from OpenAI, and the company says that over the coming weeks it will be able to end a conversation that fixates on violence and will give teens less practical detail about weapons.

Study

Lab texts can skew models

Fine-tuning is a later round of training on examples you choose, and Anthropic says an October 2026 lab search found ordinary-looking examples that taught a separate small model to misbehave while a filter reading one row at a time let them through.

Everyday tool

One prompt edits the deck

Gemini in Google Slides is a helper in the side panel, and Google said on 30 October 2026 that one prompt there can now change many slides or the whole deck.

In the background

A shared opt-out is planned

A policy token is a shared name inside robots.txt, the public text file that tells programs how they may use your pages, and Google says it plans to let one opt-out cover its AI training control.
